docs.title: Faraday Cli
docs.text: Use Faraday directly from your favorite terminal. faraday-cli is the official client that makes automating your security workflows easier.

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Two ways to use it — an interactive shell or single commands for scripts and pipelines
  • Import tool output — process reports from 100+ security tools (Faraday Plugins), or run a supported tool and upload its results automatically
  • Workspaces, hosts, services and vulnerabilities — list, create, update and delete them, with stats and a workspaces dashboard
  • AI pentests with FaradAI — launch FaradAI scans and triage from the terminal, including self-registration on the FaradAI-scan SaaS
  • Agents and scanners — run local Faraday Agents (runners) and server-side cloud agents (scanners)
  • Several servers — saved connection sessions to switch between servers or users
  • Executive reports — generate them from your templates (commercial versions of Faraday)

docs.title: Command overview
docs.text:
Command What it does auth, status Connect to a Faraday server and manage saved sessions workspace List, create, select, enable/disable workspaces and show a dashboard host, service, vuln Query and manage a workspace's data tool report, tool run Import a tool report, or run a tool and import its output stats Vulnerability statistics pentest, triage, faradai FaradAI scans, triage and FaradAI-scan SaaS registration scanners List and run server-side cloud agents agent (runners) List and run local Faraday Agents executive_report Generate executive reports set, help, version Settings, help and version

See Commands for every option.

docs.title: Examples
docs.text: Here you have some snippets of different workflows you can generate using faraday-cli

docs.title: One-line Continuous Scan
docs.text:
Scan the assets of a workspace with nmap and import the results back.

$ faraday-cli host list -ip -w other_ws | nmap -iL - -oX /tmp/nmap.xml && faraday-cli tool report -w other_ws /tmp/nmap.xml

Info

In this case there should be a workspace named "other_ws" with hosts in it.

docs.title: AI pentest with FaradAI
docs.text:
Launch an AI-driven pentest against a target using the FaradAI cloud agent (scanner) and watch it to completion.

$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://example.com --watch

Info

pentest is the shortcut for faradai scan. Use --advanced for the deeper 80-round audit, triage -w <workspace> to re-test the findings of a workspace, or scanners run <id|name> to run any cloud agent with its own parameters. See Commands.

docs.title: One-line nmap scan of all the hosts in the workspace
docs.text:
To scan all the hosts inside a workspace with nmap and import the results back to faraday.

$ for ip in $(faraday-cli host list -ip); do faraday-cli tool run "nmap -Pn -p443,80 -sV --script=+http-enum -vvv $ip"; done

docs.title: Scan your subdomains
docs.text:
Use a tool like assetfinder to do a domains lookup, scan them with nmap and send the results to faraday

$ assetfinder -subs-only example.com| sort | uniq |awk 'BEGIN { ORS = ""; print " {\"target\":\""}
{ printf "%s%s", separator, $1, $2
separator = ","}END { print "\"}" }' | faraday-cli agent run -a 1 -e nmap --stdin

Info

For this purpose, an agent is created and already connected to run the nmap executor.

docs.title: Send Faraday Executive Reports by mail
docs.text:
Run a daily scan and send your report

$ faraday-cli executive_report create -t "generic_default.docx (generic) (Word)" --confirmed -d /tmp/report.docx && echo "Faraday Daily Report" | mail -s "Daily Report" user@example.com -A /tmp/report.docx

docs.title: Load your assets from your cloud provider
docs.text:
Here you can list your assets using a cli from your provider (in this example Digital Ocean), then generate a json with that information and use faraday-cli to send it to faraday.

$ doctl compute droplet list --format PublicIPv4,Name --no-header | awk 'BEGIN { ORS = ""; print " ["}
{ printf "%s{\"ip\": \"%s\", \"description\": \"%s\"}", separator, $1, $2
separator = ", "}END { print "] " }' | faraday-cli host create --stdin

docs.title: Commands
docs.text:
All the commands can be run in Shell Mode (type faraday-cli and then the command) or in Command Mode (faraday-cli <command> ...).

Getting help

  • faraday-cli --help shows the common commands and examples.
  • faraday-cli help -v lists every command; faraday-cli help <command> or faraday-cli <command> -h shows a command's options (e.g. faraday-cli scanners run -h).

Quoting arguments in Command Mode

Quote arguments the same way you would for any other CLI:

$ faraday-cli tool run "nmap -sV www.example.com"
$ faraday-cli host create -d '[{"ip": "10.0.0.1", "description": "web server"}]'
$ faraday-cli scanners run --agent "First Scan" -w my_workspace

The older escaped syntax shown in previous versions of these docs (tool run \"nmap ...\", -d \''[...]'\') is still accepted, so existing scripts keep working. You can also pass the whole command as a single string: faraday-cli "workspace list".

docs.title: Command aliases
docs.text:
Some command groups can be typed with more than one name:

Command Also available as agent (local Faraday Agents) agents, runner, runners scanners (cloud agents) scanner faradai scan pentest faradai triage triage tool, workspace, host, service, vuln tools, workspaces, hosts, services, vulns

docs.title: auth
docs.text:
Authenticate with your faraday server. Each login is saved as a named session and becomes the active connection.

$ faraday-cli auth
Faraday url [http://localhost:5985]: http://localhost:5985
User: faraday
Password:
Saving config (session 'faraday@localhost')
✔ Authenticated with faraday: http://localhost:5985

If the user has 2FA enabled you will be asked for the OTP code.

Optional arguments:

Syntax Description -f/--faraday-url FARADAY_URL url of your faraday server -i/--ignore-ssl Ignore SSL certificate validation -u/--user USER Faraday user -p/--password PASSWORD Faraday password -n/--name NAME Session name to save this connection as (default: user@host)

One active connection, multiple saved sessions

faraday-cli keeps one active connection at a time, but remembers the others as named sessions so you can switch between them instead of being logged in to two servers at once. Logging in with auth (and faradai verify/login, which save a faradai-scan session) adds a session and makes it active. Sessions are stored in ~/.faraday-cli.yml (see Settings).

docs.title: auth list
docs.text:
List the saved connection sessions (the active one is marked). Session names default to user@host, so two users on the same server each get their own switchable session instead of overwriting each other.

$ faraday-cli auth list
  ID  ACTIVE    NAME                          KIND    SERVER                              USER          WORKSPACE
----  --------  ----------------------------  ------  ----------------------------------  ------------  ------------
   1  ✔         alice@faraday.example.com     server  https://faraday.example.com/        alice         -
   2            bob@faraday.example.com       server  https://faraday.example.com/        bob           ws_b
   3            faradai-scan                  saas    https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com    you@corp.com  ext_corp_com

Optional arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: auth use
docs.text:
Switch the active connection to a saved session — by its ID number, its name, or its user/email (when unique). Every command (including pentest/triage/scanners) then uses it.

$ faraday-cli auth use 3                 # by ID
$ faraday-cli auth use faradai-scan      # by name
$ faraday-cli auth use you@corp.com      # by user/email
Switched to 'faradai-scan' as you@corp.com (https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com) — workspace ext_corp_com

docs.title: auth rm
docs.text:
Remove a saved session (by ID, name or user). If it was the active one, you are left without an active connection until you auth use another session or run auth again.

$ faraday-cli auth rm 2
Removed 'bob@faraday.example.com'.

Faraday token expiration

You may want to change the faraday token expiration time, so you don't have to authenticate so often.

The default is 12 hours.

To do it, change the value of api_token_expiration (expressed in seconds) in your faraday server.ini

docs.title: status
docs.text:
Show the status of your current connection — the Faraday server, its version, your user, whether the token is valid, the active workspace and the CLI version. When you have more than one saved session, they are listed below.

$ faraday-cli status
FARADAY SERVER                IGNORE SSL    SERVER VERSION    USER     VALID TOKEN    WORKSPACE    CLI VERSION
----------------------------  ------------  ----------------  -------  -------------  -----------  -------------
https://faraday.example.com/  False         corp-5.25.0       alice    ✔              test         2.3.0

Saved sessions (switch with 'auth use <name>'):
  ID  ACTIVE    NAME                       KIND    SERVER                            USER          WORKSPACE
----  --------  -------------------------  ------  --------------------------------  ------------  ------------
   1  ✔         alice@faraday.example.com  server  https://faraday.example.com/      alice         test
   2            faradai-scan               saas    https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com  you@corp.com  ext_corp_com

If the server can't be reached or answers with an error, status shows the reason (e.g. Could not validate authentication: Server error (502)) instead of failing.

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: workspace list
docs.text:
List workspaces created in faraday.

$ faraday-cli workspace list -p
+--------+---------+------------+---------+----------+----------+------------+
| NAME   |   HOSTS |   SERVICES | VULNS   | ACTIVE   | PUBLIC   | READONLY   |
|--------+---------+------------+---------+----------+----------+------------|
| test   |      13 |         13 | 39      | True     | False    | False      |
+--------+---------+------------+---------+----------+----------+------------+

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -j/--json-output Show output in json -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -i/--show-inactive Include inactive (disabled) workspaces

docs.title: workspace get
docs.text:
Get details of a workspace.

$ faraday-cli workspace get -p test
+--------+----------+----------+------------+---------+------------+---------+
| NAME   | ACTIVE   | PUBLIC   | READONLY   |   HOSTS |   SERVICES |   VULNS |
|--------+----------+----------+------------+---------+------------+---------|
| test   | True     | False    | False      |      13 |         13 |      39 |
+--------+----------+----------+------------+---------+------------+---------+

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -j/--json-output Show output in json -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: workspace create
docs.text:
Create a new workspace in faraday. The new workspace becomes the active one unless you pass -d.

$ faraday-cli workspace create test_workspace
✔ Created workspace: test_workspace

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -d/--dont-select Don't select the workspace after creating it

docs.title: workspace select
docs.text:
Select your active workspace. Unless you use the -w argument, all the commands will use this workspace. The active workspace is stored with the active session and shown in the shell prompt ([ws:test]>).

$ faraday-cli workspace select test
✔ Selected workspace: test

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: workspace delete
docs.text:
Delete workspace from faraday.

$ faraday-cli workspace delete test
Deleting workspace: test
Deleted workspace: test

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: workspace disable
docs.text:
Disable (deactivate) a workspace. Disabled workspaces are hidden from workspace list unless you pass -i/--show-inactive.

$ faraday-cli workspace disable test

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: workspace enable
docs.text:
Enable (reactivate) a disabled workspace.

$ faraday-cli workspace enable test

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: host list
docs.text:
List hosts in a workspace.

$ faraday-cli host list -p
+------+------------+---------+-------------+------------+---------+
|   ID | IP         | OS      | HOSTNAMES   |   SERVICES |   VULNS |
|------+------------+---------+-------------+------------+---------|
|   11 | 127.0.0.1  | unknown |             |          1 |       3 |
|    3 | 127.0.0.10 | unknown |             |          1 |       3 |
|    6 | 127.0.0.11 | unknown |             |          1 |       3 |
+------+------------+---------+-------------+------------+---------+

Use -ip to print only the IPs, one per line (handy to pipe into other tools):

$ faraday-cli host list -ip -w test | nmap -iL - -oX /tmp/nmap.xml

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json -ip/--show-ip Show ip only

docs.title: host create
docs.text:
Create hosts from a JSON list.

$ faraday-cli host create -w test -d '[{"ip": "10.0.0.1", "description": "web server"}]'
Created host

Info

You can pass the host data via stdin. 

$ echo '[{"ip": "1.1.1.5", "description": "some text"}]' | faraday-cli host create --stdin

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -d/--host-data HOST_DATA Host data in json format --stdin Read host-data from stdin --resolve-hostname Resolve the hostname of each host when it is created

host data schema: 

{'type': 'array', 'items': {'type': 'object', 'properties':
    {'ip': {'type': 'string'}, 'description': {'type': 'string'},
    'hostnames': {'type': 'array'}}, 'required': ['ip', 'description']}}

docs.title: host delete
docs.text:
Delete host.

$ faraday-cli host delete 13
Host deleted

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description host_id ID of the host

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: service list
docs.text:
List services in a workspace.

$ faraday-cli service list -p
+------+--------+--------------+------------+--------+------------+--------+---------+
|   ID | NAME   | SUMMARY      | IP         |   PORT | PROTOCOL   |   HOST |   VULNS |
|------+--------+--------------+------------+--------+------------+--------+---------|
|    1 | ssh    | (22/tcp) ssh | 127.0.0.8  |     22 | tcp        |      1 |       2 |
|    2 | ssh    | (22/tcp) ssh | 127.0.0.3  |     22 | tcp        |      2 |       2 |
|    3 | ssh    | (22/tcp) ssh | 127.0.0.10 |     22 | tcp        |      3 |       2 |
+------+--------+--------------+------------+--------+------------+--------+---------+

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json

docs.title: vuln list
docs.text:
List vulnerabilities from a workspace, 50 per page by default. In interactive mode you can move between pages with + (next), - (previous) and q (exit).

$ faraday-cli vuln list -p
+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------+----------+-------------+--------------------------------------------------+-------------+
|   ID | NAME                                                                        | SEVERITY   | STATUS   | CONFIRMED   | ASSET                                            | HOSTNAMES   |
|------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------+----------+-------------+--------------------------------------------------+-------------|
| 5200 | Terminal Services Encryption Level is Medium or Low                         | med        | opened   | False       | 10.33.112.22 [Service - (3389/tcp) msrdp]        | qa3app02    |
| 5198 | Microsoft Windows Remote Desktop Protocol Server Man-in-the-Middle Weakness | med        | opened   | False       | 10.33.112.22 [Service - (3389/tcp) msrdp]        | qa3app02    |
| 5120 | SMB Signing Disabled                                                        | med        | opened   | False       | 10.33.112.24 [Service - (445/tcp) cifs]          | qa3app04    |
| 5272 | Ethernet Card Manufacturer Detection                                        | info       | opened   | False       | 10.33.112.21 [Host - ID:72]                      | qa3app01    |
+------+-----------------------------------------------------------------------------+------------+----------+-------------+--------------------------------------------------+-------------+
[Next Page: '+', Previous Page: '-', Exit: 'q']

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json --severity [SEVERITY ...] Filter by severity: informational/critical/high/medium/low/unclassified --confirmed Show only confirmed vulnerabilities --ignore-info Ignore informational/unclassified vulnerabilities --page PAGE Page number to display, starting from 0 --limit LIMIT Number of vulnerabilities per page (default 50, max 4000) --no-interaction Don't ask for page navigation (useful in scripts) --advanced-filters FILTER Apply complex filters using a JSON structure, e.g. --advanced-filters '{"filters":[{"name":"description","op":"like","val":"%sql injection%"}]}'

docs.title: vuln update
docs.text:
Update one or more fields of a vulnerability.

$ faraday-cli vuln update 46 -w test --status closed
Vulnerability updated

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description vulnerability_id ID of the vulnerability

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name --status STATUS Status of the Vulnerability: open, closed, re-opened, risk-accepted --severity SEVERITY Severity of the Vulnerability: unclassified, info, low, med, high, critical --desc DESCRIPTION Description --name NAME Vulnerability Name --tag TAG Tag to add to the vuln (repeat it to add more than one) --confirmed CONFIRMED Indicates if the Vulnerability is confirmed: True, False

docs.title: vuln delete
docs.text:
Delete a vulnerability.

$ faraday-cli vuln delete 46 -w test
Vulnerability deleted

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description vuln_id ID of the vulnerability

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: vuln add-evidence
docs.text:
Add an image evidence to a vulnerability.

$ faraday-cli vuln add-evidence -id 46 -w test ~/evidence.png
Evidence upload was successful

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description -id/--vulnerability-id VULNERABILITY_ID ID of the vulnerability image Image path

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name

docs.title: tool report
docs.text:
Process different tools reports and upload the information into faraday.

Info

Check our Faraday Plugins repo for information about compatible tools.

$ faraday-cli tool report $HOME/Downloads/openvas-report.xml
📄 Processing Openvas report
⬆ Sending data to workspace: test
✔ Done

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description report_path Path of the report file

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name --create-workspace If the workspace given with -w doesn't exist, create it --plugin-id PLUGIN_ID Plugin ID (force detection) -j/--json-output Show output in json (don't send it to faraday) --vuln-tag VULN_TAG Tag to add to vulnerabilities (repeatable) --host-tag HOST_TAG Tag to add to hosts (repeatable) --service-tag SERVICE_TAG Tag to add to services (repeatable) --min-severity SEVERITY Minimum severity of vulnerabilities to import (unclassified/info/low/med/high/critical) --max-severity SEVERITY Maximum severity of vulnerabilities to import (unclassified/info/low/med/high/critical)

docs.title: tool run
docs.text:
Execute a tool and upload the information into faraday. Quote the whole tool command so it reaches faraday-cli as a single argument.

Info

Check our Faraday Plugins repo for information about compatible tools.

$ faraday-cli tool run "nmap www.exampledomain.com"
💻 Processing Nmap command
Starting Nmap 7.80 ( https://nmap.org ) at 2021-02-22 14:13 -03
Nmap scan report for www.exampledomain.com (10.196.205.130)
Host is up (0.17s latency).
rDNS record for 10.196.205.130: 10.196.205.130.bc.googleusercontent.com
Not shown: 996 filtered ports
PORT     STATE  SERVICE
80/tcp   open   http
443/tcp  open   https
2222/tcp open   EtherNetIP-1
3306/tcp closed mysql

Nmap done: 1 IP address (1 host up) scanned in 11.12 seconds
⬆ Sending data to workspace: test
✔ Done

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description command Command of the tool to process

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name --create-workspace If the workspace given with -w doesn't exist, create it --plugin-id PLUGIN_ID Plugin ID (force detection) -j/--json-output Show output in json (don't send it to faraday) --vuln-tag VULN_TAG Tag to add to vulnerabilities (repeatable) --host-tag HOST_TAG Tag to add to hosts (repeatable) --service-tag SERVICE_TAG Tag to add to services (repeatable) --min-severity SEVERITY Minimum severity of vulnerabilities to import (unclassified/info/low/med/high/critical) --max-severity SEVERITY Maximum severity of vulnerabilities to import (unclassified/info/low/med/high/critical) --force Process the output of the command regardless of its result

docs.title: stats
docs.text:
Different stats about the vulnerabilities in Faraday.

$ faraday-cli stats --type severity -w test

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description --type {severity,vulns,date} Type of stat

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name --ignore-info Ignore informational/unclassified vulnerabilities --severity [SEVERITY ...] Filter by severity: informational/critical/high/medium/low/unclassified --confirmed Confirmed vulnerabilities

docs.title: Agents
docs.text:
Info

For these commands you need to have our Faraday Agents configured.

runner / runners alias

Faraday Agents (the local dispatcher runners) are also reachable as runner/runners (and agents) — runners list, runners get, runners run are synonyms for the agent commands below. The server-side scanners live under the separate scanners group.

docs.title: agent list
docs.text:
List all configured agents.

$ faraday-cli agent list
  ID  NAME    ACTIVE    STATUS    EXECUTORS
----  ------  --------  --------  -----------
   2  nico    True      online    nmap

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json

docs.title: agent get
docs.text:
Get information of an agent and its executors.

$ faraday-cli agent get 2
   ID  NAME    ACTIVE    STATUS
----  ------  --------  --------
   2  nico    True      online

Executors:
  ID  NAME    PARAMETERS [REQUIRED]
----  ------  -----------------------
   2  nmap    target [True]
              option_pn [False]
              option_sc [False]
              option_sv [False]
              port_list [False]
              top_ports [False]
              host_timeout [False]
              script_timeout [False]

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description AGENT_ID ID of the Agent

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format -j/--json-output Show output in json

docs.title: agent run
docs.text:
Run an executor.

$ faraday-cli agent run -a 1 -e nmap -w my_workspace -p '{"target": "www.google.com"}'
Running executor: unnamed_agent/nmap
Parameters: {"TARGET": "www.google.com"}
Generated Command: 13

Info

You can pass the executor parameters via stdin. 

$ echo '{"target": "www.google.com"}' | faraday-cli agent run -a 1 -e nmap --stdin --workspace-name my_workspace
If no -p or --stdin argument is provided, then the executor parameters will be asked one by one.

You can store the parameters in env variables and will be auto loaded.

Example: 

For the TARGET parameter of the NMAP executor save the variable FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TARGET

You can store the parameters in a file and use it as a 'profile' to repeat scans 

$ cat scan_test.com_nmap.vars
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TARGET=test.com
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_OPTION_PN=true
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_OPTION_SC=false
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_OPTION_SV=true
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_PORT_LIST=
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TOP_PORTS=
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_HOST_TIMEOUT=
FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_SCRIPT_TIMEOUT=

$ source scan_test.com_nmap.vars && faraday-cli agent run -a 2 -e nmap -w test
Running executor: unnamed_agent/nmap
Parameters: {"TARGET": "test.com", "OPTION_PN": "true", "OPTION_SC": "false", "OPTION_SV": "true"}
Generated Command: 14

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description -a/--agent-id AGENT_ID ID of the agent -e/--executor-name EXECUTOR_NAME Executor name

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -p/--executor-params EXECUTOR_PARAMS Executor params in json (otherwise read from --stdin, env variables or asked one by one) --stdin Read executor-params from stdin -w/--workspace-name WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name (default: the active workspace) --vuln-tag VULN_TAG Tag to add to vulnerabilities --host-tag HOST_TAG Tag to add to hosts --service-tag SERVICE_TAG Tag to add to services --min-severity SEVERITY Minimum severity of vulnerabilities to import (unclassified/info/low/med/high/critical) --max-severity SEVERITY Maximum severity of vulnerabilities to import (unclassified/info/low/med/high/critical)

docs.title: Scanners (cloud agents)
docs.text:
Info

Scanners are Faraday cloud agents (the v3/cloud_agents API) — the server-side security agents, distinct from the local Faraday Agents / runners above. This is the generic group: list any cloud agent and run it with its own parameters. FaradAI is one such scanner, so it can be launched here (scanners run faradai ...) or via its own richer faradai command. scanner is an alias of scanners.

docs.title: scanners list
docs.text:
List the cloud agents (scanners) available on the server.

$ faraday-cli scanners list
  ID  NAME                SLUG        CATEGORY    LAST_RUN
----  ------------------  ----------  ----------  --------------------------------
   7  FaradAI             faradai     AI Pentest  2026-10-16T19:52:07.004347+00:00
   6  New CVEs Detection  top-10-cve  discovery   2026-10-16T12:47:49.051544+00:00

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -j/--json-output Show output in json -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: scanners get
docs.text:
Show a single cloud agent and the parameters it accepts (useful before scanners run so you know which --param keys to pass).

$ faraday-cli scanners get 7
  ID  NAME     SLUG     CATEGORY    LAST_RUN
----  -------  -------  ----------  --------------------------------
   7  FaradAI  faradai  AI Pentest  2026-10-16T19:52:07.004347+00:00

Parameters (pass with --param KEY=VALUE):
PARAM               REQUIRED    TYPE/DESC    DEFAULT
------------------  ----------  -----------  ----------------------
GOAL                            string       Open ports
MODE                            string       claude
ROUNDS                          integer      1
TARGET              yes         string       example.com
INSTRUCTION         yes         string       Are there any open port?
TIME_LIMIT_SECONDS              integer      111

The DEFAULT column shows the values stored on the agent.

Required Arguments:

Syntax Description scanner_id ID of the cloud agent

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -j/--json-output Show output in json -p/--pretty Show table in a pretty format

docs.title: scanners run
docs.text:
Launch any cloud agent against one or more workspaces with its parameters. The agent is selected by id or by a name/slug fragment, given positionally or with -a.

$ faraday-cli scanners run faradai -w my_workspace \
    --param TARGET=https://example.com --param ROUNDS=20
Launching cloud agent faradai
  Workspaces: my_workspace
  Params:     {'TARGET': 'https://example.com', 'ROUNDS': 20}
Run launched. Command id(s): 158
Reproduce this run with:
  faraday-cli scanners run --agent faradai -w my_workspace --param TARGET=https://example.com --param ROUNDS=20

# equivalent, params as a JSON object
$ faraday-cli scanners run -a 7 -w my_workspace \
    --params-json '{"TARGET": "https://example.com", "MODE": "Dual", "ROUNDS": 20}'

Guided mode (wizard): if you don't pass any parameter on an interactive terminal (or you pass --wizard), the CLI lists the agent's parameters and asks for each one, pre-filling the values stored on the agent. Before launching it shows the final parameters and asks for confirmation (default No), and afterwards it prints a one-liner to repeat the run without prompts.

$ faraday-cli scanners run faradai -w my_workspace

Parameters for faradai (Enter = keep default/skip):
  GOAL — string
    GOAL [Open ports]:
  TARGET [required] — string
    TARGET [example.com]: https://app.example.com
  ...
Launching cloud agent faradai
  Workspaces: my_workspace
  Params:     {'GOAL': 'Open ports', 'TARGET': 'https://app.example.com', ...}
Launch this run? [y/N]: y
Run launched. Command id(s): 159

Without a terminal (scripts, CI), no questions are asked: pass the parameters with --param/--params-json.

Arguments:

Syntax Description AGENT / -a/--agent AGENT Cloud-agent id or name/slug fragment (e.g. 7, faradai, "First Scan"). Required, positionally or with -a -w/--workspace WORKSPACE Workspace name (repeatable) --param KEY=VALUE Run parameter (repeatable). Bare integers and true/false are converted. --params-json PARAMS_JSON All run params as one JSON object (alternative to repeated --param) --wizard Ask for the parameters interactively, even if --param was given --watch Poll the launched command(s) until they finish

Which workspace is used

The run goes to: the -w workspace(s) → a workspace passed as a parameter (e.g. --param WORKSPACES=ws, used by FaradAI Triage) → the active workspace → on a terminal, you are asked (pre-filled with the agent's default). If none can be resolved, the CLI asks you to pass --workspace.

Only executor inputs go in --param

A cloud agent has two kinds of fields: its executor run inputs (e.g. First Scan's targets, FaradAI's TARGET) and its stored configuration (resolve_hostname, ignore_info, tags, default workspaces…). Only run inputs may be passed with --param — configuration is set on the agent itself in the Faraday web UI. The CLI validates your --param keys against the agent's input schema before launching and lists the accepted keys on a mismatch (scanners get <id> shows them too).

--watch

After launching, --watch polls the workspace's command list every ~15s and prints each command as it finishes, then Run finished.. Press Ctrl-C to stop watching — the run keeps going server-side. Some cloud agents keep their command "In progress" on the server after the scan is done; in that case check the results in the Faraday web UI and stop watching with Ctrl-C.

docs.title: FaradAI
docs.text:
Info

FaradAI is a Faraday cloud agent (a scanner), with its own command for the common cases: tiered scans, triage, and the FaradAI-scan SaaS onboarding. To list cloud agents use scanners list; to run FaradAI with raw parameters use scanners run faradai.

Shortcuts

The two common actions have top-level shortcuts: faraday-cli pentest (= faradai scan) and faraday-cli triage (= faradai triage). All the flags below apply to the shortcut too.

Which server is used

faradai scan / faradai triage run against your active connection (see auth) — your Faraday server, or the FaradAI-scan SaaS if you switched to its session with auth use faradai-scan.

  • If you have saved sessions but none is active, the CLI asks you to pick one with auth use <id|name>.
  • If nothing is configured at all, the first pentest/triage on a terminal walks you through creating a FaradAI-scan SaaS account (see below). Without a terminal (scripts, CI) it fails and tells you to run auth or faradai login.
  • --standalone is deprecated: it switches the active connection to the faradai-scan session for the run. Prefer auth use faradai-scan.

Register with an email on the domain you're scanning

A self-registered SaaS account is scoped to ext_<your-email-domain> and can only scan that domain and its subdomains. Registering you@gmail.com (or any public provider, or another company's domain) to scan faradaysec.com will be rejected — public providers get no scan scope at all. During the guided onboarding the CLI checks your email against the --target and, if they don't match, stops before sending the code (no account is created). An already-registered account is checked the same way before a scan launches (Out of scope: …). Use an email at the target's domain, or have an operator authorize the target and re-run with --skip-scope-check (the server still enforces scope).

docs.title: faradai scan
docs.text:
Launch a FaradAI pentest against a target. The FaradAI cloud agent is auto-discovered by name/slug; pass --agent-id to select it explicitly.

# shortcut
$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://example.com

# full form
$ faraday-cli faradai scan --target https://example.com --workspace my_workspace
Launching FaradAI scan
  Target:     https://example.com
  Mode:       Dual
  Rounds:     20 (standard)
  Workspaces: my_workspace
Scan launched. Command id(s): 151

$ faraday-cli faradai scan --target https://example.com -w my_workspace --advanced --watch
Parameter Description --target TARGET URL/host to scan (required) -w/--workspace WORKSPACE Workspace name (repeatable); see below for the default --instruction INSTRUCTION Pentest instruction (default: the FaradAI wizard's staged template for the tier — standard or advanced) --goal GOAL Free-text goal/focus for the run (default: the wizard's GOAL for the tier) --mode {Dual,Claude,Codex} Execution mode (default: Dual) --rounds ROUNDS Max agent rounds (default: 20 standard; 80 with --advanced). Explicit --rounds overrides the count but not the template. --advanced Advanced (deeper) scan — 80 rounds + the wizard full-audit instruction, instead of the standard 20 --agent-id AGENT_ID Explicit cloud-agent id (skips FaradAI auto-discovery) --watch Poll the launched command(s) until they finish (see --watch) --skip-scope-check Skip the client-side target-vs-ext_<domain> workspace pre-check (operator-authorized workspaces; the server still enforces scope) --standalone (deprecated) Switch to the faradai-scan session for the run; prefer auth use faradai-scan

Workspace

You rarely need --workspace for a scan: without it the active workspace is used, and when there is none and you have access to exactly one workspace (the usual case for a SaaS scan user), that one is used. Pass --workspace when you can access several.

Instructions match the web wizard

faradai scan (standard/advanced) and faradai triage launch with the same staged instruction templates the FaradAI web wizard sends — standard → standard, --advanced → full-audit, triage → triage. Override with --instruction for a custom run.

docs.title: faradai triage
docs.text:
Run a FaradAI triage over the existing findings of one or more workspaces (re-test/reproduce, enrich, optionally auto-close false positives). This targets the separate FaradAI Triage cloud agent (auto-discovered); triage has no --target — it works over the --workspace findings, not a URL. If none of the workspaces has findings, it refuses to launch (unless you pass --dry-run).

# shortcut
$ faraday-cli triage --workspace my_workspace --severities critical,high --reproduce

# full form
$ faraday-cli faradai triage --workspace my_workspace --severities critical,high --reproduce
Parameter Description -w/--workspace WORKSPACE Workspace to triage (repeatable, at least one required) --severities SEVERITIES Comma-separated severities (e.g. critical,high,medium) --confirmed-only Only triage findings already marked confirmed --auto-close-fp Auto-close findings determined to be false positives --target-filter TARGET_FILTER Only triage findings matching this target/host filter --reproduce Actively re-test (reproduce) each finding against the live target --batch-size BATCH_SIZE Findings per triage batch --rounds ROUNDS Max agent rounds --goal GOAL Free-text goal for the triage run --instruction INSTRUCTION Triage instruction (default: the wizard's staged triage template) --agent-id AGENT_ID Explicit cloud-agent id (skips auto-discovery) --watch Poll the launched command(s) until they finish --standalone (deprecated) Switch to the faradai-scan session for the run --dry-run Ask the agent to plan without changing findings

docs.title: FaradAI-scan SaaS (register / verify / login)
docs.text:
Info

The FaradAI-scan SaaS (https://faradai-scan.apps.faradaysec.com) lets you self-register from the CLI — no Faraday web UI. New accounts get one free scan per tier; further scans need purchased credits.

Zero-to-scan flow:

$ faraday-cli faradai register --email you@corp.com
Verification code sent to you@corp.com.
Generated password: ****************  (save it — you'll log in with it later)
Run: faradai verify <code>

$ faraday-cli faradai verify 123456
FaradAI scan account ready — active connection is now 'faradai-scan' (you@corp.com).

$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://corp.com

Or skip straight to scanning — with nothing configured, the first pentest/faradai scan on a terminal walks you through register + verify inline, then runs:

$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://corp.com
No FaradAI-scan account yet — let's create one.
Email: you@corp.com
Verification code sent to you@corp.com.
Generated password: ****************  (save it — you'll log in with it later)
Verification code (check your email): 123456
Launching FaradAI scan ...

register keeps the email + password until you verify, so verify needs only the code. Pass --password to choose your own; omit it and one is generated for you and printed once (save it — it's what you log in with later). Returning users re-authenticate without a new code:

$ faraday-cli faradai login --email you@corp.com
Password:
Logged in to https://scan.apps.faradaysec.com — active connection is now 'faradai-scan'. Workspace: ext_corp_com

verify and login save the SaaS connection as the faradai-scan session and make it the active connection, so every command (pentest, triage, scanners, vuln, …) runs against the SaaS until you switch back with auth use <name>. They also store your ext_<domain> workspace, so later scans need only --target. The pending email/password are removed from the config once verify succeeds (or when the server says there is no pending registration).

Command Parameters faradai register --email (required), --password, --dashboard-url faradai verify CODE (positional, or --code; required), --email and --password (default: the pending registration), --dashboard-url (default: the one used by register) faradai login --email (required), --password (asked if omitted), --scan-url

docs.text:

$ faraday-cli executive_report list-templates -p

docs.title: executive_report create
docs.text:
Generate an executive report with a given template.

$ faraday-cli executive_report create -t "generic_default.html (generic) (PDF)" --title title --summary summary --enterprise company -d /tmp/test.pdf --ignore-info
Report created: /tmp/test.pdf

Optional Arguments:

Syntax Description -w/--workspaces-names WORKSPACE_NAME Workspace name -t/--template TEMPLATE Template (see list-templates) --title TITLE Report title --summary SUMMARY Report summary --recommendations RECOMMENDATIONS Report recommendations --conclusions CONCLUSIONS Report conclusions --scope SCOPE Report scope --objectives OBJECTIVES Report objectives --enterprise ENTERPRISE Enterprise name --confirmed Confirmed vulnerabilities --severity [SEVERITY ...] Filter by severity: informational/critical/high/medium/low/unclassified --ignore-info Ignore informational/unclassified vulnerabilities -d/--destination DESTINATION Report destination

docs.title: Interactive shell features
docs.text: When you run faraday-cli with no arguments you get an interactive shell (Faraday>, or [ws:<workspace>]> once a workspace is selected) with command history, tab completion and these extras:

docs.title: Auto-command detection
docs.text:
Anything you type that isn't a faraday-cli command is run as an OS command. If auto_command_detection is enabled (the default) and the command belongs to a tool supported by Faraday Plugins (e.g. nmap, ping), its output is also processed and uploaded to the active workspace:

[ws:test]> nmap 10.0.0.1
💻 Processing Nmap command
...
⬆ Sending data to workspace: test
✔ Done

If there is no active workspace the command just runs. Turn it off with set auto_command_detection false to run OS commands without processing them. The same detection applies in command mode (faraday-cli nmap 10.0.0.1); use tool run to choose the workspace, tags or plugin explicitly.

docs.title: cd
docs.text:
Change the current working directory of the shell (cd alone goes to your home).

[ws:test]> cd /tmp

docs.title: Update notifications
docs.text:
On startup, faraday-cli checks PyPI and shows a message when a newer version is available; status shows it too in the CLI VERSION column.

A new version of faraday-cli (2.3.1) is available!!

docs.title: help
docs.text:
Using the help command you can get info of any command.

$ faraday-cli help -v

Documented commands (use 'help -v' for verbose/'help <topic>' for details):

Core
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
auth                  Authenticate with a faraday server (or manage sessions: list/use/rm)
exit                  exit the application. Shorthand: Ctrl-D.
status                Show Cli status
version               Faraday cli version

Objects
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
agent                 agent actions
executive_report      executive_report actions
faradai               faradai actions
host                  host actions
scanners              scanners (cloud agent) actions
service               service actions
tool                  tool actions
vuln                  vulnerabilities actions
workspace             workspace actions

Stats
------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
stats                 Different statistics about the information on Faraday
...

$ faraday-cli help auth
usage: auth [-h] [-f FARADAY_URL] [-i] [-u USER] [-p PASSWORD] [-n NAME]
            {list,rm,use} ...

Authenticate with a faraday server (or manage sessions: list/use/rm)

options:
  -h, --help            show this help message and exit
  -f, --faraday-url FARADAY_URL
                        Faraday server URL
  -i, --ignore-ssl      Ignore SSL verification
  -u, --user USER       Faraday user
  -p, --password PASSWORD
                        Faraday password
  -n, --name NAME       Session name to save this connection as (default:
                        user@host)

action:
  {list,rm,use}
    list                list saved connection sessions
    rm                  remove a saved connection session
    use                 switch the active connection

The same help is available as faraday-cli <command> -h, also for subcommands (faraday-cli auth list -h).

docs.title: version
docs.text:
Show the faraday-cli version.

$ faraday-cli version
faraday-cli: 2.3.0

docs.title: set
docs.text:
List or change the CLI settings. See Settings.

$ faraday-cli set ignore_info_severity true
ignore_info_severity - was: False
now: True

docs.title: history
docs.text:
In shell mode, list, re-run, edit or save the commands you typed before (they are kept in ~/.faraday-cli_history).

[ws:test]> history
    1  workspace select test
    2  vuln list --severity critical
[ws:test]> history -r 2

docs.title: exit / quit
docs.text: Exit the interactive shell (also Ctrl-D).

docs.title: Installation Instructions
docs.text:
Before installing, we recommend creating and activating a Python virtual environment to avoid affecting your system Python packages. For example:

python3 -m venv .venv
source .venv/bin/activate

You can also use virtualenv if you prefer. Once the virtual environment is active, run the installation commands below.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
pip 
$ pip install faraday-cli
git 
$ git clone https://github.com/infobyte/faraday-cli.git
$ cd faraday-cli
$ pip install .

Python version

Python 3.10 or later is recommended (the CLI is tested on Python 3.10 to 3.12).

docs.title: Authenticate with your Faraday server
docs.text:
$ faraday-cli

Faraday url [http://localhost:5985]:

Password:
Saving config (session 'faraday@localhost')
✔ Authenticated with faraday: http://localhost:5985

In scripts, pass everything as arguments (add -i to skip SSL verification, e.g. for a self-signed certificate):

$ faraday-cli auth -f https://faraday.example.com -u faraday -p "$FARADAY_PASSWORD" -i

More than one server

Each login is saved as a named session (user@host). If you work with more than one Faraday server (or user), run auth for each one and switch with auth list / auth use <id|name>. Check the connection with status.

docs.title: Create a workspace or select active Workspace
Process reports from any of the many tools we support
Filter and tag what you import
docs.text:
tool report and tool run can skip vulnerabilities by severity and tag what they import:

# skip informational findings
$ faraday-cli tool report scan.xml --min-severity low

# only critical and high
$ faraday-cli tool report scan.xml --min-severity high

# tag vulnerabilities, hosts and services (repeat a flag to add more tags)
$ faraday-cli tool report scan.xml --vuln-tag q4-scan --host-tag production --service-tag external

docs.title: Or let FaradAI find it
docs.text:
If your Faraday server has the FaradAI cloud agent, launch an AI pentest against a target and its findings land in the workspace:

$ faraday-cli pentest --target https://example.com -w test
Launching FaradAI scan
  Target:     https://example.com
  Mode:       Dual
  Rounds:     20 (standard)
  Workspaces: test
Scan launched. Command id(s): 151

faraday-cli scanners list shows every cloud agent available on your server, and faraday-cli triage -w test re-tests the findings of a workspace. Don't have a Faraday server? The first pentest walks you through creating a FaradAI-scan SaaS account. See FaradAI and Scanners.

docs.title: Or run the tools with faraday-cli
docs.text:
Faraday Cli can be used in two modes:

  • shell mode: faraday-cli reacts as a shell to your commands
  • command mode: faraday-cli reacts as a command with parameters

docs.title: Global settings
docs.text:
You can list or change some settings from the cli itself with set.

$ faraday-cli set
Name                    Value                           Description
--------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
allow_style             Terminal                        Allow ANSI text style sequences in output (valid values:
                                                        Always, Never, Terminal)
always_show_hint        False                           Display tab completion hint even when completion suggestions
                                                        print
auto_command_detection  True                            Enable/disable automatic command detection
custom_plugins_path     None                            Path of custom plugins folder
echo                    False                           Echo command issued into output
editor                  vi                              Program used by 'edit'
feedback_to_output      False                           Include nonessentials in '|', '>' results
hostname_resolution     False                           Resolve hostname
ignore_info_severity    False                           Ignore Informational vulnerabilities from reports and
                                                        commands
max_completion_items    50                              Maximum number of CompletionItems to display during tab
                                                        completion
quiet                   False                           Don't print nonessential feedback
scripts_add_to_history  True                            Scripts and pyscripts add commands to history
timing                  False                           Report execution times

$ faraday-cli set ignore_info_severity true
ignore_info_severity - was: False
now: True

The faraday-cli specific settings are:

Setting Default Description custom_plugins_path None Path where the cli will look for custom Faraday Plugins ignore_info_severity False If True, informational vulnerabilities are ignored in reports and commands auto_command_detection True If True, the cli processes and uploads the output of any supported tool you run (see Auto-command detection) hostname_resolution False If True, resolve hostnames when processing tool output

custom_plugins_path, ignore_info_severity and auto_command_detection are saved in the configuration file and kept between runs. The rest of the settings (including hostname_resolution) only last for the current session.

The other settings in the list (allow_style, echo, editor, quiet, timing…) are the standard ones of the interactive shell library (cmd2).

docs.title: Configuration file
docs.text:
faraday-cli stores its configuration in ~/.faraday-cli.yml. Use the FARADAY_CLI_CONFIG environment variable to point it to another file (handy to keep separate configurations or to test without touching yours):

$ FARADAY_CLI_CONFIG=~/faraday-cli-lab.yml faraday-cli auth

The file contains:

  • sessions — every saved connection (server URL, token, SSL setting, active workspace, user), and active_session, the one in use. Manage them with auth list/auth use/auth rm.
  • auth / faraday — a copy of the active connection and workspace, kept for compatibility with older versions.
  • settings — the saved settings described above.
  • faradai_scan — the FaradAI-scan SaaS endpoints and, while a registration is pending, its email and password (removed once faradai verify succeeds).

A configuration file from an older version (a single auth block) is migrated automatically to a session named after the server host.

Warning

The file holds API tokens (and, during a SaaS registration, a password), so faraday-cli writes it readable by your user only (0600). Don't share it or commit it to a repository.

docs.title: Environment variables
docs.text: Variable Default Description FARADAY_CLI_CONFIG ~/.faraday-cli.yml Path of the configuration file FARADAY_CLI_TIMEOUT 10000 Timeout of each request to the Faraday server, in seconds FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_<EXECUTOR>_<PARAM> — Default value of an executor parameter for agent run (e.g. FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TARGET); see agent run

docs.title: Example: CI/CD pipeline
docs.text:
In a pipeline there is no one to answer prompts, so pass everything as arguments or environment variables:

# keep the pipeline's config apart from yours
export FARADAY_CLI_CONFIG="$CI_PROJECT_DIR/.faraday-cli.yml"

faraday-cli auth -f https://faraday.example.com -u scanner -p "$SCANNER_PASSWORD"
faraday-cli workspace select production-scan

# import a report generated earlier in the pipeline, tagged with the build
faraday-cli tool report scan.xml --vuln-tag "build-$CI_PIPELINE_ID" --min-severity low

# or run an agent executor with its parameters from the environment
export FARADAY_CLI_EXECUTOR_NMAP_TARGET=10.0.0.0/24
faraday-cli agent run -a 1 -e nmap
